description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Engineering Materials topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: engineering-materials

facts.claim: Main classes: metals, ceramics, polymers (and semiconductors, composites)

source.quote: The main classes of materials are metals, semiconductors, ceramics and polymers

facts.claim: A crystal is an ordered, repeating arrangement of atoms

source.quote: crystal structure is a description of the ordered arrangement of atoms, ions, or molecules in a crystalline material

facts.claim: Described by a unit cell and lattice parameters

source.quote: The lengths of principal axes/edges, of the unit cell and angles between them are lattice constants

facts.claim: Gives ultimate tensile strength, breaking strength, elongation, reduction in area

source.quote: Properties that are directly measured via a tensile test are ultimate tensile strength, breaking strength, maximum elongation and reduction in area

facts.claim: A specimen is pulled in tension until it fails

source.quote: a sample is subjected to a controlled tension until failure

facts.claim: Hardness = resistance to localised plastic deformation (indentation)

source.quote: hardness (antonym: softness) is a measure of the resistance to localized plastic deformation

facts.claim: Scratch, indentation and rebound hardness

source.quote: There are three main types of hardness measurements: scratch, indentation, and rebound

facts.claim: Fatigue: crack growth under cyclic loading

source.quote: fatigue is the initiation and propagation of cracks in a material due to cyclic loading

facts.claim: Fast fracture when the stress intensity exceeds fracture toughness

source.quote: occurs when the stress intensity factor of the crack exceeds the fracture toughness of the material

facts.claim: Shows which phases exist at given conditions; lines are phase boundaries

source.quote: lines of equilibrium or phase boundaries, which refer to lines that mark conditions under which multiple phases can coexist at equilibrium

facts.claim: Austenite (γ, FCC) is stable above the eutectoid temperature 727 °C

source.quote: austenite exists above the critical eutectoid temperature of 1000 K (727 °C)

facts.claim: Austenite is face-centred cubic and dissolves more carbon (up to ~2%)

source.quote: can dissolve considerably more carbon (as much as 2.03% by mass at 1,146 °C

facts.claim: TTT diagrams plot temperature against (log) time for isothermal transformation

source.quote: are plots of temperature versus time (usually on a logarithmic scale)

facts.claim: Stainless steel has ≥ 10.5% chromium, forming a passive film

source.quote: Stainless steel's resistance to corrosion comes from its chromium content of 10.5% or more

facts.claim: Heat treatment alters properties by controlled heating and cooling

source.quote: Heat treatment involves the use of heating or chilling, normally to extreme temperatures, to achieve the desired result, such as the softening or hardening

facts.claim: Quenching hardens; tempering, annealing and normalising are other treatments

source.quote: Heat treatment techniques include annealing, case hardening, precipitation strengthening, tempering, carburizing, normalizing and quenching

facts.claim: Case hardening adds carbon to the surface: hard skin, tough core

source.quote: combines much of the malleability and toughness of a low-carbon steel core with the hardness and resilience of the outer high-carbon steel skin

facts.claim: Two or more constituents with different properties combined

source.quote: is a material which is produced from two or more constituent materials

facts.claim: Matrix (binder) plus reinforcement (fibres or particles)

source.quote: made up of a binding agent forming the matrix and a filler material (particulates or fibres)

facts.claim: Properties change in a controlled way with external stimuli

source.quote: have one or more properties that can be significantly changed in a controlled fashion by external stim
